issues.legal_issue: Interim relief in a public interest proceeding must be granted only after applying the relevant injunction safeguards and balancing the consequences for all affected interests.
material_facts: The High Court passed interim directions in a public interest challenge to amended development regulations before the writ petition had been finally heard.
Interested mill owners and other affected parties had intervened, but their affidavits had not yet been filed and they had not been given a full opportunity to respond.
The challenged directions could affect workers, financial institutions, mill owners and third-party purchasers, and delay had allowed transactions and investments to advance.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that an interim order, particularly in a public interest proceeding, requires consideration of a prima facie case, balance of convenience and irreparable injury, along with the applicable public interest litigation principles. An order affecting a person should normally not be made without a hearing; ex parte relief is exceptional. The court must also weigh the possibility that refusing relief would defeat the petition against the losses and hardships that granting it may cause.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the injunction factors and exceptional-circumstances test in Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund v. Kartick Das and Andhra Bank v. Official Liquidator; the public interest litigation principles in Dr. B. Singh v. Union of India and Dattaraj Nathuji Thaware v. State of Maharashtra; and the principles on exceptional interim relief, terms and undertakings, and delay defeating equity in Deoraj v. State of Maharashtra, Raunaq International Ltd. v. I.V.R. Construction Ltd., Guruvayoor Devaswom Managing Committee v. C.K. Rajan, Chairman & MD BPL Ltd. v. S.P. Gururaja, Narmada Bachao Andolan v. Union of India, and R & M Trust v. Koramangala Residents Vigilance Group.

predicates.interim_relief_in_public_interest_procee: A party seeks interim relief in a proceeding brought in the public interest.
predicates.affected_interests_may_suffer_harm: The interim order may cause loss or hardship to people or entities whose interests are affected by it.
predicates.affected_person_not_heard: A person whose interests would be affected has not yet had an opportunity to be heard.
predicates.relief_may_have_irreversible_effect: Granting or withholding interim relief may effectively determine the practical outcome or cause harm that cannot readily be undone.

issues.definition: When interim relief is sought in a public interest proceeding and affected interests may suffer harm, the court must assess the injunction factors and balance consequences, with particular care if an affected person has not been heard or the relief may have irreversible effects.

issues.legal_issue: Advanced transactions undertaken under a rehabilitation scheme may proceed during a challenge to the governing development regulations if the arrangement protects the possibility of effective relief should the challenge succeed.
material_facts: The National Textile Corporation had negotiated transactions concerning seven mills, and the transactions had reached a final stage.
The purchasers of one mill had already paid substantial consideration, and completion of the transactions would release substantial funds.
Stopping the transactions risked stalling a rehabilitation scheme and causing further interest and other hardship to workers and financial institutions.
The Corporation could, if necessary, offer vacant land from other mills if the writ petition ultimately succeeded.
issues.conclusion: The Court permitted the National Textile Corporation to complete the transactions under the rehabilitation scheme, subject to offering vacant land available from other mills for adjustment if necessary should the writ petition succeed.
issues.legal_principle: Applying the principles governing interim relief and the balance of hardship, including those discussed in Deoraj v. State of Maharashtra and Raunaq International Ltd. v. I.V.R. Construction Ltd., the Court fashioned a conditional arrangement that allowed advanced transactions to proceed while preserving the possibility of relief in the pending proceeding.

predicates.appeal_from_interim_order_in_public_inte: The matter is an appeal concerning an interim order in a public interest proceeding.
predicates.transactions_near_completion: Transactions under a rehabilitation arrangement have reached an advanced stage.
predicates.stopping_transactions_would_harm_workers: Stopping the transactions would impede rehabilitation and cause hardship to workers, creditors or other affected interests.
predicates.alternative_land_can_be_adjusted_if_chal: Vacant land from other properties can be offered for adjustment if the pending challenge succeeds.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns interim relief in a public interest proceeding, advanced rehabilitation transactions would cause hardship if stopped, and alternative land can preserve effective relief, the transactions may proceed subject to that adjustment.

issues.legal_issue: Applications for development permissions may be processed during a pending challenge, but approvals and construction must comply with applicable law and no construction may proceed under new applications while the challenge remains pending.
material_facts: Some mills had already received development sanctions, commencement permissions or permissions for particular stages of work.
In some cases, applications had been entertained despite the expiry of the applicant's lease.

The Court directed that statutory authorities process relevant applications strictly according to law and that applicants establish ownership and comply with applicable schemes, rules, regulations and by-laws.
The Court permitted new applications for approvals to be processed but prohibited construction under those new approvals.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed statutory authorities to process applications strictly in accordance with law, not to grant permission to a person lacking ownership of the land, and to ensure compliance with applicable development controls. New applications could be processed, but no construction could be carried out pursuant to them pending the proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the requirements of lawful statutory decision-making and compliance with the development-control scheme under the Maharashtra Regional and Town Planning Act, 1966, and the regulations, rules and by-laws made under it.

predicates.appeal_from_interim_order_in_public_inte: The matter is an appeal concerning an interim order in a public interest proceeding.
predicates.development_permission_applications_are_: Applications for permission to develop land or continue development work are pending before statutory authorities.
predicates.construction_would_rely_on_new_approval: The proposed construction would proceed under an approval sought through a new application during the pending proceeding.

issues.definition: When development applications are pending in an appeal concerning interim relief, authorities may process them lawfully, but construction relying on new approvals must not proceed.

issues.legal_issue: Further construction and creation of third-party rights during a pending challenge must be undertaken at the owners’ risk and made expressly subject to the eventual court orders, with public notice of specified future activity.
material_facts: Mill owners and interveners proposed further construction and creation of third-party interests while the validity of the amended development regulations remained under challenge.
The Court allowed such activity only subject to the pending proceedings and directed public notice before further construction or creation of third-party interests pursuant to fresh permissions.
The Court also directed that future agreements creating third-party rights state that enforcement is subject to further orders of the High Court.
issues.conclusion: Before further construction or creation of third-party interests pursuant to fresh permissions, the owners or interveners had to publish notice in widely circulated English and Marathi newspapers. Future agreements had to make enforcement subject to further court orders, and the activity would be at the owners’ risk, without any claim to equity, and subject to the court’s orders.
issues.legal_principle: The Court used conditions and safeguards in shaping interim relief, consistently with the principles in Raunaq International Ltd. v. I.V.R. Construction Ltd. and Guruvayoor Devaswom Managing Committee v. C.K. Rajan that appropriate terms may be imposed to protect affected interests and address potential loss if the proceeding succeeds.

predicates.appeal_from_interim_order_in_public_inte: The matter is an appeal concerning an interim order in a public interest proceeding.
predicates.owners_intend_further_construction_or_th: Owners or interested persons intend to carry out further construction or create third-party interests while the challenge remains pending.

issues.definition: When owners intend further construction or creation of third-party rights during a pending challenge in an interim appeal, that activity must be publicized and made subject to court orders at the owners’ risk.

issues.legal_issue: Public authorities directed to produce relevant documents must place them before the court, and withholding a relevant document may justify an adverse inference or another appropriate order.
material_facts: The High Court directed the State and municipal authority to produce documents under multiple headings.
The directions had been made without hearing those authorities and without considering the practical hardship of producing a large volume of documents.
The Supreme Court required the authorities to place all relevant documents before the High Court while leaving the High Court free to respond appropriately if relevant documents were withheld.
issues.conclusion: The State and municipal authority were required to place all relevant documents before the High Court; if a relevant document was later found to have been withheld, the High Court could draw an adverse inference or make another appropriate order.
issues.legal_principle: The Court tailored the document-production direction to account for the authorities’ hardship while preserving the High Court’s ability to address the withholding of relevant material through an adverse inference or another appropriate order.

predicates.appeal_from_interim_order_in_public_inte: The matter is an appeal concerning an interim order in a public interest proceeding.
predicates.public_authorities_hold_documents_releva: Public authorities possess documents relevant to the case pending before the court.

issues.definition: When public authorities hold documents relevant to a pending public interest case, they must produce them, and withholding relevant material may support an adverse inference.
